<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen-api-reference.ts from sdk/openapi.json. Do not edit — including in Studio; the next build replaces this file. -->

::api-operation{method="PATCH" path="/v1/businesses/{biz}/dunning_policies/{dpol}"}
#docs
A new `config` replaces the whole stored set and applies to every customer on the policy from their next dunning step.

## Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `biz` | `string` | **yes** | Business id (biz_…) |
| `dpol` | `string` | **yes** | The dpol. |

## Headers

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | `string` | no | Safely retry writes — repeats return the original response. If a write FAILED after it had already taken effect, that failure is what repeats: the key is spent, and a new attempt needs a new key. |

## Body

The request body is **required**.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | no | The name operators see. |
| `code` | `string` | no | A unique code among live policies. |
| `description` | `string` | no | An optional description. |
| `config` | `object` | no | The per-invoice dunning keys of `dunning_config` (enabled, mode, retries, final_action, dunning_period_days, skip_retries_for_hard_failures, park_hard_declines, adaptive_timing, minimum_amounts, dun_offline_invoices, dun_one_time_invoices, dun_trial_and_future_subscriptions, retries_by_method, adaptive_cadence). Absent keys take the defaults; the policy stores the full set. Business-wide keys are refused. |
| `expected_version` | `integer` | no | Optimistic concurrency: current resource_version; 409 on mismatch |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Updated |
| `400` | Invalid body |
| `404` | No such dunning policy |
| `409` | The code is in use, or a version conflict |

#request
```bash [Request]
curl -X PATCH "$TMBILLING_URL/v1/businesses/biz_XXXXXXXXXXXX01/dunning_policies/Dpol" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TMBILLING_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Brightwater Analytics",
    "description": "Everything a growing team needs."
  }'
```
